title: KPMG M&A Outlook 2027: From market resilience to renewed deal activity
gist: Oxford Economics and KPMG Germany surveyed 200+ German M&A decision-makers and found German M&A resilient in 2026, driven by US-led inbound interest in industrial and tech assets. The outlook is cautiously positive, with deal counts forecast to rise through 2028 on SME succession, international investment and public spending, while AI adoption in M&A processes has doubled. The public page is a short summary of a gated report.

insights.claim: German M&A activity proved resilient in 2026 despite weak domestic growth, higher borrowing costs and geopolitical disruption, per an Oxford Economics/KPMG Germany survey of 200+ M&A decision-makers.
insights.speaker: Suki Masana
insights.so_what: Deal flow in Germany has decoupled somewhat from weak macro; advisory/PE activity there may hold up better than GDP suggests.
insights.quote: German M&A proved resilient in 2026 despite weak domestic growth, higher borrowing costs, and geopolitical disruption.

insights.claim: International buyers were a key driver of German M&A in 2026, led by US investors seeking German industrial and technology assets.
insights.speaker: Suki Masana
insights.so_what: Cross-border (especially US-led) inbound demand for German industrial/tech targets supports valuations of German Mittelstand-type assets.
insights.quote: International interest was particularly strong, led by US investors seeking German industrial and technology assets.

insights.claim: The 2027 outlook for German M&A is cautiously positive: nearly half of surveyed respondents expect German M&A activity to increase.
insights.speaker: Suki Masana
insights.so_what: Sentiment among German corporates, PE funds and family offices points to a modest pickup rather than a boom.
insights.quote: Nearly half of respondents expect German M&A activity to increase.
insights.locator: The outlook for 2027 is cautiously positive

insights.claim: Oxford Economics modelling forecasts German M&A deal counts to rise through 2028.
insights.speaker: Suki Masana
insights.so_what: A multi-year upswing in German deal counts would benefit M&A advisers, PE exit/entry windows and transaction-related services.
insights.quote: Our modelling forecasts deal counts to rise through 2028
insights.locator: The outlook for 2027 is cautiously positive

insights.claim: Three forces are expected to support rising German deal counts: SME succession needs, international investment, and the gradual effect of public spending.
insights.speaker: Suki Masana
insights.so_what: Succession-driven sales of SMEs create structural supply of targets independent of the cycle, while fiscal spending works with a lag.
insights.quote: supported by SMEs succession, international investment, and the gradual effect of public spending
insights.locator: The outlook for 2027 is cautiously positive

insights.claim: AI is changing both how and why M&A deals are pursued in Germany; adoption of AI in M&A processes has doubled.
insights.speaker: Suki Masana
insights.so_what: AI is becoming both a process tool and a deal rationale, potentially accelerating due diligence and driving tech-capability acquisitions.
insights.quote: Adoption in M&A processes has doubled, although most firms still rely on general-purpose tools.
insights.locator: AI is also changing how and why

insights.claim: Despite doubled AI adoption in M&A processes, most firms still rely on general-purpose AI tools rather than specialised ones.
insights.speaker: Suki Masana
insights.so_what: There is headroom for specialised M&A/due-diligence AI tooling as adoption matures.
insights.locator: AI is also changing how and why
